definition: The US export-control measure of an AI chip's compute: roughly dense TFLOPS (or TOPS) times the bit width of the operation. Chips at or above 4,800 TPP need a licence to ship to China.
TPP divided by die area in mm². Added by the October 2023 rule so a vendor cannot dodge the TPP line by spreading the same compute over more silicon.
The US Commerce Department agency that writes and licenses export controls, including the AI-chip rules aimed at China.
A product variant cut down to sit just below an export-control threshold (for example A800, H800, H20), so it can ship without a licence until the rule changes.
A licence condition under which the exporter pays part of its sales revenue to the US government: 15% on H20 (Aug 2025) and 25% on H200 (Dec 2025) China sales.
Geographic revenue assigned to the country where the customer is headquartered rather than where it is billed. NVIDIA switched to this basis in Q3 FY2026, which raised China's reported share.
Huawei's family of AI accelerators (910B/910C, 950PR/950DT, 960, 970), sold mainly in China with the CANN software stack and SuperPoD rack-scale systems.
A market where a vendor can sell everything it can make. A lost customer then costs little in the short run, because the capacity is resold to others.
